title: Hairy cell leukemia
subtitle: Indolent B-cell leukemia defined by BRAF V600E · splenomegaly with pancytopenia and monocytopenia · one course of a purine analog buys most patients a decade or more; the old “variant” (now SBLPN) is a different, BRAF wild-type disease
source: Compiled from primary trial reports and consensus guidelines (Hairy Cell Leukemia Foundation consensus, Grever 2017 and 2026 update; NCCN) verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Presentation
items: Rare: <2% of leukemias; middle-aged adults, strong male predominance
Splenomegaly (often massive) without adenopathy, and pancytopenia with monocytopenia — the monocytopenia is the clue on a routine CBC
Dry tap: reticulin fibrosis defeats the aspirate — diagnose on the core biopsy (interstitial “fried-egg” infiltrate) + peripheral blood flow, which finds the few circulating cells
Infections are the cause of morbidity: bacterial, fungal and atypical mycobacteria (monocytopenia + neutropenia)
Smear: small-to-medium cells with oval nuclei and circumferential hairy cytoplasmic projections

blocks.heading: Classic HCL vs its look-alikes
blocks.footnote: HCL score (CD11c, CD103, CD123, CD25): 3–4 = classic. WHO-HAEM5 dropped “HCL-variant” and folded it into splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli (SBLPN); ICC 2022 keeps HCL-v as a provisional entity.

blocks.heading: When to treat — consensus
items: Symptomatic splenomegaly, progressive cytopenias, recurrent infection or constitutional symptoms
None of these → observe; many patients sit for years
CR: Hb >11 without transfusion, platelets >100,000, ANC >1,500, no hairy cells on marrow or blood, spleen regressed. MRD by IHC or flow is prognostic but not yet a treatment target
Relapse cutoff is 2 years (raised from 1): relapse ≥2 yr after CR → retreat with purine analog; <2 yr → switch class

blocks.html: IGHV4-34 — the trap. Classic-looking HCL that is BRAF wild-type: all 13 IGHV4-34+ cases were wild-type Xi, Blood 2012. Usually unmutated, higher WBC, poor response to cladribine and shorter PFS and OS Arons, Blood 2009; MAP2K1 mutations cluster here too. A BRAF-negative “HCL” should prompt a second look.

Treat the infection first. Cladribine and pentostatin deepen neutropenia for weeks, and post-cladribine fever is common — so defer the purine analog during active infection. If counts are too low for the infection to clear, a BRAF inhibitor (vemurafenib ± rituximab) restores counts without myelosuppression and can bridge to definitive therapy — off-label.

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — the evidence, dosing and supportive care

blocks.heading: Key evidence
rows: Single 7-day infusion: CR 91%; 26% relapsed at a median 29 mo; retreatment CR 62%
The regimen that made HCL a one-course disease
Pentostatin or cladribine: CR 80%, median RFS 16 yr; no difference between drugs
Relapse continues late — 25% of 5-yr CRs relapse by 15 yr
Pentostatin is equivalent to cladribine; no excess second cancers
Cladribine daily ×5 vs weekly ×5: response 86% in both
Weekly is not less toxic (grade 3–4 neutropenia 90% vs 80%)
Cladribine + concurrent vs delayed (≥6 mo) rituximab: CR 100% vs 88% (NS); MRD-free CR 97% vs 24%; at 8 yr 94% vs 12% still MRD-free
Concurrent R buys deep, lasting MRD negativity at the cost of grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia 59% vs 9%. Survival benefit not shown
Relapsed: ORR 96–100%, CR 35–42%; RFS 19 mo in CR, 6 mo in PR
Median 3 prior lines: CR 87% (65% MRD-negative); PFS 78% at median 37 mo
The preferred non-purine regimen at relapse
CR 90%, 96% of CRs MRD-negative; no relapse at 35 mo
Not FDA-approved for HCL — the tumor-agnostic label covers solid tumors only
Anti-CD22 immunotoxin: CR 41%, durable CR 30%; HUS 7.5%, capillary leak 5%
Withdrawn from the US market in 2023 (commercial decision)

blocks.heading: Dosing
rows: 0.14 mg/kg/day IV over 2 h, days 1–5 (NIH: 0.15 mg/kg), or 0.1 mg/kg/day continuous IV ×7 days, or 0.14 mg/kg weekly ×5 — one course
Cladribine 0.15 mg/kg days 1–5 + rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly ×8, concurrent from day 1 (or delayed ≥6 mo)
4 mg/m² IV every 2 weeks until best response; hydrate; hold for renal dysfunction
Vemurafenib 960 mg PO BID ×8 weeks + rituximab 375 mg/m² ×8 doses over 18 weeks
Dabrafenib 150 mg BID + trametinib 2 mg daily

blocks.heading: Monitoring and supportive care
items: Prolonged CD4 lymphopenia after purine analogs — median ~40 months to recover → PJP and HSV/VZV prophylaxis
Irradiated blood products indefinitely after a purine analog (transfusion-associated GVHD) BSH 2020
Neutropenic fever in ~42% after cladribine. Routine G-CSF not recommended: it shortened neutropenia (9 vs 22 days) but did not cut fever or admissions
Vemurafenib: rash, photosensitivity, arthralgia, cutaneous SCC / keratoacanthoma — dermatology checks. Dab/tram: pyrexia
Inactivated vaccines before therapy; no live vaccines

blocks.heading: Splenic small B-cell differential
rows: CD25+ CD103+ CD123+ CD11c bright, annexin A1+, BRAF V600E; monocytopenia
CD103+ but CD25−, annexin A1−, BRAF wild-type, MAP2K1; leukocytosis, prominent nucleoli
Polar (villous) projections, CD103 usually −, CD25 variable, annexin A1−; NOTCH2 / KLF2; may have a small IgM paraprotein
Villous cells, red-pulp pattern, CD25−, annexin A1−; CCND3 mutations; BRAF wild-type
CD5+ — CD23+ (CLL) or cyclin D1+ (MCL) — HCL and its look-alikes are CD5−
blocks.footnote: Annexin A1 + BRAF V600E together settle classic HCL; everything else in this list is negative for both.

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: Splenomegaly + monocytopenia + dry tap = HCL until proven otherwise
BRAF V600E is the diagnosis and the target. Wild-type → think SBLPN or IGHV4-34
Cure-like, not cure: relapse keeps happening late but responds to retreatment
Moxetumomab is gone (2023) — don't list it as an option
